# Narration technology: assessment, pronunciation solution and cost comparison

*Prepared 7 November 2026. Nothing in this document was tested against a paid speech service: no API key was used and no audio was generated by Gemini or Google Cloud. Findings come from reading the code and from the providers' published pages (linked). Prices change, and several of these models are in preview: re-check before any spending is approved.*

## 1. What the original Story Spark narrator actually is

| Question | Answer (from the code) |
|---|---|
| Engine | The **browser's built-in speech engine** (`window.speechSynthesis` / `SpeechSynthesisUtterance`) in `StorySpark.tsx`, `StoryReader.tsx` and `src/lib/story-spark/narration.ts`. It is **not** Gemini. |
| Voice | Whatever voice the *device* has. `pickVoice()` prefers names containing natural / neural / online / google / enhanced / premium, then en-GH, en-NG, en-GB, then any English. So quality varies by phone, laptop and browser, and the same story can sound different on every device. |
| Cost | Free. Runs on the device. |
| Pronunciation control | **None, apart from changing the spelling of the text sent to the voice.** The Web Speech API has no SSML or phoneme support in browsers. |
| Word highlighting | Uses the engine's `boundary` events when they arrive; falls back to *estimated* timing on devices that never send them (many mobile browsers). That is why it is never presented as verified sync. |
| Why it sounds clearer than the new preview | The new preview deliberately uses a **free placeholder** voice (espeak-ng) so that word timing could be exact without any paid service. It is robotic by design and is labelled as a placeholder. Device voices (especially Google/Microsoft neural ones) are better. |

## 2. The existing Gemini integration

* `src/ai/genkit.ts`: Genkit with `googleAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY })`; default model `googleai/gemini-3-flash-preview`.
* **Text-to-speech exists, but only for the math modules:** `generateTTSAction` (two copies, `src/ai/flows/junior-actions.ts` and `src/app/dashboard/junior-actions.ts`) calls `googleai/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` with five prebuilt voices (Puck, Algenib, Achernar, Enif, Kore), returns 24 kHz mono WAV, and charges **1 school AI credit per call**. It is called from `math-modules-a.tsx`. Story Spark does not use it.
* **Image generation exists:** `generateLessonImageAction` calls `googleai/imagen-4.0-fast-generate-001` at 5 credits per image. A third-party report says the Imagen 4 endpoints may be shut down from 17 August 2026 ([tokencost.app](https://tokencost.app/blog/imagen-4-shutdown-gemini-3-1-flash-image-cost)); that date has passed, so **this action should be checked and may already be failing**. I have not changed it.

## 3. Can Gemini TTS give natural Ghanaian-English narration with accurate names?

From Google's [Gemini-TTS documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/docs/gemini-tts):

* **Accent and style:** controllable by a natural-language prompt (accent, pace, tone, emotion). Supported English locales listed: en-US, en-IN (GA); en-AU, en-GB (preview). **No en-GH, en-NG or en-KE is listed.** So "Ghanaian English" can be *requested in the prompt* but is not a guaranteed, named voice.
* **Pronunciation control:** the page documents pace control and structured verbalisation of things like dates and addresses. It does **not** document SSML, phonemes, IPA or custom pronunciations. The only lever for a name is **words in the prompt** ("say Efua as three syllables, roughly eh-FOO-ah"), which is probabilistic and can vary from one take to the next.
* **Timestamps:** word timestamps are **not documented**. Word-level highlight would need separate alignment plus human verification.
* **Limits:** about 4,000 bytes of text per field, about 655 seconds of audio per request. Fine for sentence- or page-sized clips.

**Conclusion:** Gemini TTS is likely the most *expressive and natural* option, and it is already wired in. It cannot be *guaranteed* to pronounce Ghanaian names correctly, and tone in Akan names cannot be expressed by any of these engines. Whether it does well enough is an empirical question that only a native-speaker listening test can answer. I did not run that test.

## 4. Other engines

* **Google Cloud Text-to-Speech** ([pricing](https://cloud.google.com/text-to-speech/pricing)): Standard / WaveNet (4 USD per million characters), Neural2 (16), Chirp 3 HD (30), Studio (160). SSML `<phoneme>` with IPA is, to my understanding, supported on the older voice families; **verify per voice before relying on it**. It cannot work until a native speaker supplies verified IPA for each name. These voices are less expressive than Gemini TTS.
* **Others** (for example Azure neural voices, ElevenLabs) were not evaluated. Any would need the same listening test and a data-protection check.
* **A human narrator** is the only option that is correct on names by construction, and the best option for a flagship story. Quotes are needed; I have not invented a price.

## 5. Recommended pronunciation solution

1. **Pre-generate narration; never synthesise at read time.** The reader already plays audio files with timing. Cost is then paid once per story, not per child.
2. **Make every sentence its own clip** (implemented: `pronunciation/regeneration.ts`). A wrong name in one sentence regenerates that sentence only. Page timing is recomposed from the clips and re-validated.
3. **Keep the written spelling untouched; apply pronunciation only to what the engine is given** (implemented: `pronunciation/apply.ts`). Respelling for engines that only read text; prompt hints for Gemini; SSML phonemes only where verified IPA exists. The token count never changes, so word timing stays aligned to the written words.
4. **Native-speaker verification is the gate** (implemented: `needs-native-review` blocks published audio; `pronunciationBlockers()` lists what is outstanding). Nothing in the starter dictionary is verified.
5. **Run a small audition first** (needs your approval; see section 6): the seven requested names plus one Efua page through two or three engines, scored by two or more native speakers. If no engine passes for a name, record that name (or the whole story) with a human narrator.
6. **Timing:** because each sentence is a separate clip, sentence boundaries are exact. Word-level highlighting for Gemini/Cloud clips needs forced alignment (an open-source aligner can run locally at no cost) **plus** a human check. Until then the reader shows sentence-level highlighting only, as designed.

## 6. Cost comparison (arithmetic from `src/lib/story-library/premium-cost.ts`, prices as of 2026-11-07)

Assumptions (mine, not quotes): Efua is about 3,200 characters and 300 seconds of audio; three takes per sentence; the 65-story catalogue averages 2,400 characters and 220 seconds; images use 3 candidates per shot, 25% retries and 2 candidates for each character/setting reference sheet.

**Narration, one story (three takes):**

| Engine | Efua | 65 stories (list price, ignoring free tiers) |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS (preview) | about $0.45 | about $22 |
| Gemini 2.5 Flash TTS | about $0.23 | about $11 |
| Cloud TTS Chirp 3 HD | about $0.29 (free within 1M chars/month) | about $14 |
| Cloud TTS Neural2 | about $0.15 | about $7.50 |
| Cloud TTS WaveNet / Standard | about $0.04 | about $2 |

**Illustrations:**

| Model | Efua (13 shots, 65 images) | 65 stories (about 48 images each) |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, 1K | about $4.36 | about $209 |
| Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, 2K | about $6.57 | about $315 |
| Imagen 4 Fast | about $1.30 (**reported retired**) | about $62 |

Image prices for Gemini 3.1 Flash Image are a third party's calculation from published token counts (a floor: input and thinking tokens excluded; batch pricing reported at half) ([tokencost.app](https://tokencost.app/blog/imagen-4-shutdown-gemini-3-1-flash-image-cost), [Imagen pricing](https://pricepertoken.com/imagen-pricing)). I could not open Google's own Gemini API pricing page from this environment, so verify there.

**What this means.** Machine generation is cheap: Efua's audio and images together are under about $7, and the whole 65-story programme is in the low hundreds of dollars. **The real cost is people**: native-speaker pronunciation review, an art director approving images for consistency and dignity, cultural and curriculum reviewers, and (for the flagship) possibly a human narrator and illustrator. Plan the budget around review hours, not API fees.

**Nothing has been spent or enabled.** To proceed with the audition (about $1 for text-to-speech plus roughly $1 for a first sample image) I need your approval of the engines, the API project and billing account to use, and who will do the listening review.
